author: DAVE ONGIE\ndongie@sixriversmedia.com
title: Indians, Science Hill victorious in District 1-4A tourney
text: JOHNSON CITY — West Ridge rolled into Wednesday night's District 1-4A tournament game against top-seeded Dobyns-Bennett with momentum. The fifth-seeded Wolves picked up where they left off during a Tuesday night victory over Morristown East in a play-in game, plating two runs in the top of the first inning against the Indians. But the Tribe responded with three runs in the bottom of the first, D-B starter Walker Bishop settled in and the Indians used a six-run outburst in the fourth frame to propel them to a 13-3 run-rule victory in six innings. "They hit the ball really well last night and scored some runs," said D-B coach Ryan Wagner. "Walker gave up a couple runs early and settled in for us. It's good that we responded in the bottom of the first and regained the lead." With the win, the Tribe will face No. 2 Science Hill on Thursday evening at 5 p.m. after the Hilltoppers knocked off third-seeded Morristown West in Wednesday's nightcap. No. 5 West Ridge will play the Trojans at 7:30 p.m. in an elimination game. After the Wolves manufactured a pair of runs in a steady rain in the top of the first, the Tribe bounced right back with three runs of their own in the bottom of the frame on an RBI double by Cam Hayworth, an RBI ground out by T.J. Maxwell and a wild pitch that brought Hayworth home from third. D-B extended its lead to 4-2 in the bottom of the second when Jaylen Thomas drove a triple into the right-field corner and scored on a throwing error. The beginning of the end for West Ridge came in the bottom of the fourth when a mix of walks, errors and timely D-B hitting allowed the Tribe to post six runs and take a 10-2 lead. "We got off to a good start," said West Ridge coach Micheal Hoover. "It was nice to score early, but if you give a good team like that free bases with the walks and some defensive miscues we had right there, it just kind of snowballed on us. "We competed early and it kind of got away from us late. We'll regroup and come back ready to play tomorrow." Bishop went the distance for the Tribe, allowing just three runs on six hits in six innings of work, preserving D-B's pitching staff as they prepare to play again on Thursday. "You limit the damage, and you do what you need to do to prevent really big innings, and he did that for us," Wagner said. Taylor Blankenship came through with a two-run single for D-B while Hayworth had an RBI double and a run-scoring single. Thomas tripled and also contributed an RBI single while Andrew Reilly walked three times, picking up an RBI when he drew a walk with the bases loaded. Ty Malak led West Ridge with three hits and also drove in a run. Science Hill 7, Morristown West 0 The Hilltoppers were one out away from completing a combined no-hitter before a two-out single in the top of the seventh inning broke up the no-hit bid. Science Hill starter Levi Torbett threw five no-hit innings before giving way to Luke Edwards, who put together a pair of scoreless innings while allowing just one hit in relief. The Hilltoppers broke the game open with back-to-back three-run innings. A two-run double by Carter McKinney was the highlight of Science Hill's three-run fourth inning. The 'Toppers pushed their lead to 7-0 in the bottom of the fifth when Owen Lewis hit a three-run inside-the-park home run. Haydon Smelser finished 2-for-3 with a walk for Science Hill while McKinney was 2-for-4 and Lewis had a double to go along with his home run.

But the Tribe responded with three runs in the bottom of the first, D-B starter Walker Bishop settled in and the Indians used a six-run outburst in the fourth frame to propel them to a 13-3 run-rule victory in six innings.
